title: ContextSafe LIS export identity profile 0.1
description: Reference-only and ungoverned. The JSON shape `contextsafe import --format lis-json` reads: a synthetic laboratory result export whose identity columns (patient_id, name_to_use, pronouns, sex) become observations at the lis_return checkpoint and whose result columns (analyte, value, unit, range, flag, order, specimen) are recognized and counted but produce no observation, because the laboratory result observation family is a later item. No laboratory, interoperability, clinical, or community reviewer has approved this profile as the shape of any real export, and profile_reviewed is false on every result it produces. The column set is closed: a key outside it rejects the whole source.
$comment: JSON Schema validates structure. ContextSafe runtime validation additionally enforces the x-contextsafe-semantic-constraints below.
x-contextsafe-semantic-constraints: every row carries exactly the first row's key set
at least one of name_to_use, pronouns, or sex is present
every row's patient_id equals the case document's synthetic identifier
every cell passes the evidence boundary scan: no boundary whitespace, control or format character, PHI canary, or direct-identifier pattern
sex is read as recorded_sex_or_gender with the fixed context laboratory and never as gender_identity or sex_parameter_for_clinical_use
one observation is emitted per distinct value per identity column, so rows that disagree evaluate as ambiguous

presenceOrSyntheticToken.description: A presence state that carries no value, or the source's own synthetic token carried verbatim. An empty string is not a value and is rejected; specified without a value is ambiguous and is rejected.

resultCell.description: Recognized and counted, not observed. Empty, or a bounded token without whitespace; not interpreted by this profile.

syntheticIdentifierCell.description: An accession-shaped identifier, so synthetic only: empty, or a CSYN- or ORDER-CSYN- token.
